blocks.title: Tree
blocks.text: A tree organizes information spreading out from a main point called the root node. Each node can connect to other nodes, forming a branching structure, unlike a list, which is arranged in a straight line.

In a family tree, the oldest ancestors are the root, and each person's descendants form the next levels. Such parent-child relationships are hard to store in a straight list, so a tree is used. The book states that tree data structures were first introduced by the computer scientist John McCarthy in 1960 (Did You Know).

blocks.prompt: Why is a family tree better stored as a tree than as a list?
blocks.explanation: A list only records one straight order, while a tree records who is the parent of whom, the branching hierarchy.

items: Tree: nodes branching from a root; suits hierarchies like family trees.
